idea.description: SASRec encodes interaction histories with item and positional embeddings, causal self-attention, and feed-forward layers. It predicts the next item by scoring candidate embeddings against the sequence representation. Attention selects relevant past interactions, supporting both recent transitions and longer dependencies. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1).
idea.motivation: The paper balances the simplicity of short-context Markov models with the expressive history modeling of recurrent networks. Despite the supplied title, standard SASRec is not a dedicated cold-start method: unseen items lack trained ID embeddings, and users with little history provide limited context.
idea.implementation_notes: Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset and retain all four category models and routing. Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the supplied 200-epoch environment default. Train with shifted next-item targets, sampled-negative binary cross-entropy, and padding masks. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory and ensure the predictor writer reproduces the trained architecture. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and the compatibility interface. Select changes using only pinned macro validation HR@10; no improvement has been measured here. SASRec requires no review text, ratings, or simulator traits.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in four_categories:
    load unchanged training split
    initialize category-specific SASRec with seed 42
    for epoch in configured_epochs(default=200):
        for sequence, positive, negative in training_batches:
            features = causal_encoder(item_embedding(sequence) + position_embedding)
            loss = masked_BCE(features, positive, negative)
            update_parameters(loss)
    save model, configuration, and item mappings under trial directory
write predictor that routes categories and loads matching models
host evaluates with the pinned validation protocol

originality.positive: The original paper established self-attention as an effective sequential recommendation architecture.
originality.negative: Reusing SASRec is baseline reproduction; the supplied description proposes no distinct cold-start mechanism. Score reflects originality relative to the requested baseline, on a 1–10 scale.

future_potential.positive: Validation can assess category-specific sequence lengths, regularization, and negative sampling. Available item text could support a separately tested cold-start extension.
future_potential.negative: Benefits remain hypotheses and must fit the shared 43,200 GPU-second search budget.

code_difficulty.positive: The existing SASRec baseline and diagnostic contract provide a direct implementation starting point.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture changes require synchronized checkpoint loading, predictor generation, and diagnostic adapters. Higher scores indicate greater difficulty.

report:
Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.
